source_span: We think October is the most likely time for the next move because it is most natural to deliver hikes that the FOMC presented today as supporting "a timelier return" to the 2% target at consecutive meetings
source_chain: FOMC hiked 25bp as priced, but the dot plot came in more hawkish than Goldman expected (16-2 majority for another hike, no dissents, neutral-rate dot up to 3.25%) therefore Goldman reads the Committee as committed to a faster path back to 2% therefore Goldman adds a second hike in October to its call, on top of its unchanged December view — invalidated in that Goldman's own core PCE forecast (3.2%) already sits below the FOMC's (3.4%), so the October add is a bet on the Committee's stated urgency, not on the data Goldman itself expects to print
pulse_chain: Fed hiked 25bp as priced, but the dots surprised hawkish (16/18 want ≥1 more hike, neutral rate to 3.25%, no dissent) therefore Goldman reads this as the Committee's stated aim to return to 2% sooner via consecutive-meeting hikes therefore Goldman adds an October hike while JPMorgan holds at December alone — invalidated by prints before the Oct 28 meeting, since Goldman's own core PCE forecast (3.2%) runs below the FOMC's (3.4%), so the October call rests on Fed urgency rather than the data Goldman expects
why: The pulse reproduces Goldman's actual mechanism (hawkish dots → consecutive-meeting urgency → October add, undercut by Goldman's own lower PCE forecast) attributed to the correct bank, with JPMorgan's contrasting December-only call also correctly sourced and not reversed.
